security_audit.summary: Most Ruby backtick detections are Markdown fence false positives from documentation examples. Real risks remain in shell execution, environment inheritance, URL fetching, file writes, screenshots, raw prompt context, and generated MCP tools. The skill is educational, but these examples need stronger safety gates before production use.

remediation.suggestion: Avoid shell=True and subprocess.getoutput with interpolated strings. Pass argv arrays, validate full arguments, and enforce workspace boundaries.

remediation.issue: Generated MCP code can be loaded without review
remediation.suggestion: Require human approval, static review, sandbox tests, and rollback before connecting generated MCP servers.

remediation.issue: Screenshots can expose sensitive browser content
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit consent, redact secrets, and prevent screenshot data from leaving local context unless approved.

remediation.issue: Raw file and URL content is inserted into prompts
remediation.suggestion: Wrap untrusted content in clear boundaries and add prompt-injection handling before passing it to a model.

remediation.issue: File and network examples lack complete validation
remediation.suggestion: Validate paths under the workspace, sanitize session IDs, and add URL allowlists, timeouts, and size limits.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Through Raw Context
semantic_findings.description: ContextManager adds file and URL content directly to prompt text with no source separation, sanitization, or instruction boundary. Malicious content could steer the model toward unsafe tool use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 590-619 fetch URL content and concatenate raw file, URL, and diagnostics into the prompt. No trust boundary or prompt-injection handling is shown.

semantic_findings.title: Generated MCP Tool Hot-Loading
semantic_findings.description: The MCPAgent asks an LLM to create server code from a user description, writes it to disk, and immediately connects it. This can introduce unreviewed executable tool behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The flow explicitly generates code, saves it as a server file, and calls connect_server without a review, test, or approval gate.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Command Construction From Workspace Path
semantic_findings.description: CheckpointManager builds shell commands by interpolating the workspace path into subprocess.getoutput. A malicious workspace path could inject extra shell operations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 667-668 place workspace directly inside shell command strings. No quoting, argv execution, or path validation is shown.

content.value_statement: Autonomous coding agents need reliable loops, tools, permissions, and context handling. This skill provides pattern examples for agent loops, approvals, browser automation, checkpoints, and MCP integration.
actual_capabilities: Explains a think, decide, act, and observe loop for tool-using agents.
Shows tool schema patterns for files, terminal commands, browsers, and web search.
Presents permission levels, approval dialogs, and sandbox checks for risky actions.
Demonstrates browser automation patterns with screenshots and visual element selection.
Covers context injection, checkpoints, resume storage, and MCP server discovery.
Includes a checklist for agent safety, user experience, and implementation review.
limitations: The examples are reference patterns, not a complete production framework.
Shell, filesystem, network, and screenshot examples need strict review before use.
The skill does not provide complete tests, dependency setup, or deployment steps.
Security controls are illustrative and need environment-specific validation.

use_cases.title: Design an agent runtime
use_cases.description: Plan the core loop, model routing, tool calls, and stopping rules for a coding agent.

use_cases.title: Add safer tool approvals
use_cases.description: Map file, terminal, browser, and network actions to approval levels and user prompts.

use_cases.title: Plan MCP and browser workflows
use_cases.description: Sketch workflows for browser automation, visual reasoning, checkpoints, and MCP tool discovery.

prompt_templates.title: Map the agent loop
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new coding assistant.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use autonomous-agent-patterns to explain the basic think, decide, act, and observe loop for my coding assistant. Focus on state, tool calls, and stopping rules.

prompt_templates.title: Design tool permissions
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for safer tool use.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use autonomous-agent-patterns to design a permission model for file edits, terminal commands, browser actions, and web access. Include which actions need user approval.

prompt_templates.title: Review sandbox risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use autonomous-agent-patterns to review my planned command execution design. Identify injection, path, environment, timeout, and approval risks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan MCP tool loading
prompt_templates.prompt: Use autonomous-agent-patterns to design an MCP server discovery and generated-tool workflow. Include validation gates, rollback, tests, and human approval before loading tools.

output_examples.input: I need a safe file editing tool for a coding agent.
output: A proposed edit flow with exact-match replacement, occurrence checks, workspace path validation, and rollback support.
A permission policy that requires approval before writes and explains the changed file to the user.
A test checklist for missing files, duplicate matches, large files, and restricted paths.

output_examples.input: I want my agent to use terminal commands.
output: A command policy with allowed binaries, argument validation, timeouts, and a default approval requirement.
A warning that shell strings and inherited secrets need special handling.
A logging plan for command, working directory, exit code, stdout, and stderr.

output_examples.input: I need browser automation and MCP support.
output: A workflow that separates navigation, screenshots, visual reasoning, and user consent.
An MCP loading plan with review, test, sandbox, and rollback gates.
A context plan that marks file and URL content as untrusted before model use.

best_practices: Require explicit approval for commands, filesystem writes, generated tools, and screenshot sharing.
Keep all reads, writes, and commands inside a validated workspace boundary.
Treat file, URL, and browser content as untrusted when adding it to prompts.
anti_patterns: Running model-selected tools without a permission check.
Using shell execution with user-controlled command strings.
Loading generated MCP tools without review, tests, and rollback.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design autonomous coding agents that use tools, permissions, browser automation, context, checkpoints, and MCP integrations.

faq.question: Is this a complete agent framework?
faq.answer: No. It is a pattern guide with illustrative examples that need production engineering and security review.

faq.question: Does the skill itself execute commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation, but its examples discuss command execution and other sensitive capabilities.

faq.question: Can it help with MCP integration?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows patterns for MCP server discovery, tool registration, and generated tool workflows.

faq.question: What security review is needed?
faq.answer: Review shell execution, file writes, URL fetching, screenshot handling, prompt context, and generated tool loading.

faq.question: Does it apply to Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The patterns can guide agent designs for Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and similar tool-using systems.
